evidence_items.publisher: Gamma (press release via Venture Capital Access Online)

receipt.public_excerpt: The company has been profitable for over two years and scaled to $100 million in ARR with only $23 million in initial funding and a lean 50-person team.

evidence_items.explanation: Gamma is an AI presentation app. It said it was profitable on its own revenue in 2025, having raised little outside money. That means its price covered its costs, which goes against 'every single AI app is subsidized'.

evidence_items.locator: section 'The rent was set a year ago', paragraph 2

receipt.public_excerpt: That's how computing went from eating $2.51 for every $1 of revenue in early 2025 to 48 cents in the second quarter.

evidence_items.explanation: In early 2025, Anthropic's computing cost was about 2.5 times its revenue. That supports the claim that a major AI app, Claude, was then sold below cost and funded by outside capital.

metric_scope.metric: Compute cost as share of revenue

unresolved_gaps: Gamma's profitability is self-stated and unaudited, and the press release gives no profit figures.
Whether Gamma's costs were indirectly subsidized, because it buys model access from providers that may have priced below cost in 2025, is not settled by the evidence.
The S-1 itself could not be read; e2 relies on news coverage of it.
